title: Evaluate Bias without Manual Test Sets: A Concept Representation Perspective for LLMs

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the representational alignment differences (via cosine similarity in sparse autoencoder space) between target concepts (e.g., occupations, medical conditions) and gender reference concepts using the proposed BIASLENS framework, as well as baseline evaluations using SEAT and Perplexity tests on the WinoBias dataset.

Measuring representational alignment differences (BIASLENS) between target concepts in medical and educational domains and socioeconomic reference concepts, such as rich vs. poor, public vs. private insurance, and low-SES vs. high-SES.

Measuring representational alignment differences (BIASLENS) between medical and educational target concepts and racial reference concepts (white vs. black) in the model's internal concept representation space.
Measuring representational alignment differences (BIASLENS) between medical and educational target concepts and language/origin reference concepts (native vs. non-native, native vs. ESL).

Evaluating asymmetric correlations between target concepts (e.g., food, service, music, acting) and sentiment polarities (positive vs. negative) using BIASLENS, alongside extrinsic behavioral metrics like F1-diff, Equal Opportunity Difference (EOD), and Fairness metrics on classification tasks.
